rationale: This is largely a hybrid of two archive signals (Growth_With_Weak_Intangible_Productivity's productivity conditioner plus Plant_Buildout's ppegt growth leg) with a denominator tweak, and it introduces a mechanical coupling because ppegt enters both legs — high plant growth mechanically inflates the capital base and depresses revt/capital, so the two ranks are positively linked by construction rather than by economics.

A genuinely different conditioner (firm-specific organic top-line deceleration rather than an industry-proxy R&D dummy) with a coherent overpayment/impairment mechanism, though the author should note that acquisitions mechanically boost revt growth (so the interaction selects the residual set of acquirers still shrinking) and that low sales growth standalone is a value-like positive-return characteristic that may dampen the slope.

The reasoning explicitly claims to avoid ratio artifacts but the conditioner has the symmetric problem it disclaims — (xrd+xad)/sale falls whenever sales rise — and COALESCE-to-zero leaves the majority of non-reporting firms with an identically zero delta, creating a large rank mass point that makes the interaction degenerate to capex/ppent for much of the sample.

Labor as an investment margin is a genuinely distinct channel from the archive's capital/financing legs and is plausibly less spanned by CMA, though the reviewer should recognize that the hiring-rate anomaly is itself well documented and that zero-R&D firms all tie at the conditioner's extreme, so the signal effectively becomes employment growth within the non-innovator subsample.

This is an industry-neutralized re-run of the archive's Plant_Buildout_Without_Knowledge_Capital with a near-identical intangible leg — a standard robustness transformation rather than a new mechanism, and double-standardizing both legs will mostly shrink the spread rather than reveal a different economic effect.

The tangible-share leg equals exactly 1.0 for every firm not reporting xrd or xad, so the multiplicative form collapses to total capex/at ranked within the non-innovator subsample — i.e., a repackaging of the well-known capex/investment anomaly conditioned on a reporting dummy, which is close in spirit to the archive's tangible-buildout family.
